provenance.paper_title: Learning How to Remember: Memory Modality Selection for GUI Agents

representation_paths.memory_component: image memory: past demonstration steps kept as (instruction, raw screenshot, action)

evidence.paraphrase: Each memory candidate is a valid demonstration step holding a past GUI state and its successful action; the image form keeps the raw screenshot of that state.
Steps are embedded with Qwen3-VL-Embedding-2B and the top-1 step is retrieved once; when the image form is chosen, the full past screenshot is placed in the frozen actor's prompt.

representation_paths.memory_component: text memory: the same demonstration steps kept as (instruction, textual state description, action)

evidence.paraphrase: The text form replaces the screenshot with a textual description of the screen (UI-text annotations, element captions, or a serialized accessibility tree); a shared text-based retriever returns the same step for both forms.

derived.hybrid_relation: Each retrieved demonstration step exists as both a raw screenshot and a textual state description; a learned router chooses, per step, which form the frozen actor receives.

adjudication_notes: Community submission (corpus issue #7), reviewed against arXiv HTML v1. The issue's required modality field read Image while the author's suggested classification gave GUI primary with Image secondary; GUI is used.

Tier T1: the memory banks are built offline from successful demonstration steps (Appendix B.1: 'The memory bank is constructed once ... It is fixed before calibration and evaluation'); the agent never writes its own steps back during evaluation.

The modality router (two-layer MLP over actor hidden states and memory embeddings, Sec. 4.2, Eqs. 7-10) is trained offline with the actor frozen and stays fixed at test time. Training-time learning was not counted as T3.
